context: Zoomable circle packing of ~300 Wikipedia articles organized into 6 top-level categories (Science, Arts, History, Technology, Geography, Sports), each with 5 subcategories and 6-10 leaf articles sized by word count. Uses d3.interpolateZoom with 750ms transitions, LOD label management, breadcrumb navigation, and hover tooltips.
first_impression: The root view is immediately readable: six distinct color regions cleanly partition the space, and the nested circle structure communicates hierarchy without clutter.
what_works: The 6-color Tol Bright palette is perceptually well-separated — each category region is identifiable at a glance with no legend lookup required. LOD label management is handled well: only category names appear at root zoom, preventing label overload while still orienting the viewer.
what_doesnt: At root zoom, all leaf and subcategory size variation is invisible — hundreds of tiny dots convey no meaningful size encoding, so the word-count variable is effectively hidden until the user zooms in, making the quantitative dimension feel absent. The 'Wikipedia' label renders twice (breadcrumb and as a faded focus label inside the outer circle), which is redundant and slightly confusing at the initial state.
